# Business Network Process Genome

> A reference model of B2B operations by industry: the work, the business processes and the EDI documents that connect trading partners, with OpenText Trading Grid solutions for Retail and CPG, Automotive and Financial services.

Built by Business Network Product Management, Data and Visibility. Internal reference. Human version: https://process-genome.onrender.com/

Notes for agents:
- Concept preview for internal review. Diagrams are illustrative. Some capabilities shown are in development or planned and are not generally available. Results depend on implementation and partner participation. Names, scope and availability may change. Do not present capabilities as generally available.
- Examples describe typical operating scenarios, not specific customer accounts. Standards, versions, and mandate dates vary by partner and region. Confirm requirements with each partner before building.
- Cite the file you used.

Start with https://process-genome.onrender.com/llms-full.txt: solutions, documents, product overlay and operations in one file. Open the process files below for step-by-step business processes.

# Retail and CPG solutions on Trading Grid

Source: Business Network Process Genome, Solution overview for Retail and CPG (https://process-genome.onrender.com/#retail/solution).
Status: Concept preview for internal review. Diagrams are illustrative. Some capabilities shown are in development or planned and are not generally available. Results depend on implementation and partner participation. Names, scope and availability may change.

Retail and CPG trading relationships, connected and managed. Integrate and onboard the retailers, suppliers, carriers, 3PLs and marketplaces you trade with on Trading Grid, and monitor every document exchanged.

## Adoption path: Connect, activate, optimize, extend
Each step builds on the one before. Open a step on the Process Genome to see it across the retail documents.

### 1. Connect (Reach)
Bring retailers, suppliers, carriers, 3PLs and marketplaces onto the network, including vendors without EDI.

### 2. Activate (Completeness)
Run every document each retailer requires, from item data and orders to ship notices, invoices and sales feeds.

### 3. Optimize (Performance)
Catch late, rejected and mismatched documents before they turn into chargebacks, deductions or lost sales.

### 4. Extend (Intelligence)
Use network data and agents to predict problems and recommend actions, with a person approving each one.

## Solutions by stage

- Plan and synchronize: EDI compliance; Trading partner visibility; Item and price synchronization; Sell-through and inventory analytics; Vendor-managed inventory and replenishment
- Order and fulfill: Order-to-cash compliance; Pre-delivery document validation; Backorder and fill-rate tracking; Web EDI for suppliers; Supplier portal for retailer and CPG hubs; Drop ship and marketplace fulfillment; 3PL inventory reconciliation
- Ship and receive: Inbound shipment visibility; ASN intelligence; Chargeback prevention alerts; Receiving and three-way match; Direct store delivery reconciliation
- Settle and recover: Chargeback management; Deduction management; Supplier compliance scorecard; Returns and credit management

### Plan and synchronize
Partners, items and demand data ready before orders flow.

#### EDI compliance
- Purpose: Connect on each retailer's requirements
- Summary: Connect each vendor to the retailer as its B2B integration requirements specify, with documents tested before go-live.
- Capabilities:
  - Vendor surveys collect contacts, IDs and connection details
  - Vendors test documents against the retailer's implementation guide
  - Testing status and errors tracked by vendor until go-live
- Parties: Retailers, Vendors, Carriers
- Outcome: Vendors tested before the first order.

#### Trading partner visibility
- Purpose: Show partners the status of what you exchange
- Summary: Either side of a trading relationship can grant a limited view of the documents it exchanges on Trading Grid: a retailer to its suppliers, or a supplier to its retailers.
- Capabilities:
  - A limited view each side can grant to its trading partners
  - Documents exchanged with you, with delivery, acknowledgment and rejection status
  - Search by order, ship notice or invoice number
- Parties: Retailers, Suppliers, 3PLs
- Outcome: Both sides see the same document status.

#### Item and price synchronization
- Purpose: Synchronize item and price data
- Summary: Publish item, price and image data once, and share it with each subscribing retailer after validation.
- Capabilities:
  - GTIN, check digit and required fields validated on receipt
  - Suppliers control which retailers see their items
  - Subscribing retailers receive item updates automatically
- Parties: Suppliers, Data pools, Retailers
- Outcome: Paperless item setup and maintenance.

#### Sell-through and inventory analytics
- Purpose: Share sell-through with suppliers
- Summary: Retailers share store-level sales and inventory, and suppliers use it to plan supply, measure promotions and catch out-of-stocks early.
- Capabilities:
  - Sales and stock by item, store and week
  - Missing or late feeds flagged on arrival
  - Sell-through, in-stock and weeks of supply in ready-made analytics
- Parties: Retailers, Suppliers
- Outcome: Store-level demand visible to suppliers.

#### Vendor-managed inventory and replenishment
- Purpose: Replenish from actual sales
- Summary: Use shared sales and stock positions to recommend replenishment and track inventory against agreed targets.
- Capabilities:
  - Replenishment quantities recommended from sales and stock
  - Order handshake monitored from proposal to acceptance
  - Inventory levels tracked against agreed targets
- Parties: Retailers, Suppliers
- Outcome: Replenishment based on shared sales data.

### Order and fulfill
Orders confirmed and fulfilled across every channel.

#### Order-to-cash compliance
- Purpose: Keep orders and invoices aligned
- Summary: Check orders, acknowledgments, ship notices and invoices against each retailer's rules and timing windows, and catch late documents before they cost money.
- Capabilities:
  - Timing windows set per retailer for acknowledgments, ship notices and invoices
  - Late acknowledgments and ship notices flagged with the cause
  - Rejections by 824, 864 or email shown in the order lifecycle, with the fix
- Parties: Retailers, Suppliers, Carriers
- Outcome: Fewer rejections and late documents.

#### Pre-delivery document validation
- Purpose: Correct documents before the retailer receives them
- Summary: Check ship notices and invoices against each retailer's rules before delivery, then release each document or replace it with a corrected version.
- Capabilities:
  - Ship notices and invoices held when they break a retailer rule
  - Held documents released, or replaced with a corrected version
  - Duplicate ship notices and invoices stopped before delivery
- Parties: Suppliers, Retailers
- Outcome: Helps reduce retailer rejections and duplicates.

#### Backorder and fill-rate tracking
- Purpose: Follow short lines through to the invoice
- Summary: Compare each acknowledgment with its order to find backordered and short lines, then follow every open line through shipment and invoice.
- Capabilities:
  - Backordered and short-acknowledged lines found by comparing the 855 to the 850
  - Each open line followed through the ship notice and invoice
  - Open quantities by retailer, item and ship date
- Parties: Suppliers, Retailers
- Outcome: Short and backordered lines tracked to delivery.

#### Web EDI for suppliers
- Purpose: Trade with retailers without an EDI team
- Summary: Suppliers receive retailer orders online and turn each one into the acknowledgment, ship notice and invoice the retailer requires.
- Capabilities:
  - Prebuilt connections for major retailers and marketplaces
  - Documents filled from the order and checked against each retailer's rules
  - GS1-128 carton labels that match the ship notice
- Parties: Suppliers, Retailers, Marketplaces
- Outcome: Orders to invoices without EDI staff.

#### Supplier portal for retailer and CPG hubs
- Purpose: Bring vendors without EDI onto electronic orders
- Summary: Retailer and CPG hubs reach vendors without EDI in a web portal, where vendors confirm each line, ship with matching labels and invoice against the order.
- Capabilities:
  - Order changes and line-level confirmations tracked by vendor
  - Ship notices built from the order, with matching carton labels
  - Invoices, receipts and remittance status in one place
- Parties: Retailers, CPG hubs, Vendors
- Outcome: Vendors without EDI on electronic orders.

#### Drop ship and marketplace fulfillment
- Purpose: Ship direct to the consumer
- Summary: Run one order across EDI vendors, web-based vendors and 3PLs, with inventory and tracking returned to each channel.
- Capabilities:
  - Vendors without EDI work orders, ship notices and labels online
  - Inventory updates shared with selling channels
  - Tracking returned to the channel at shipment
- Parties: Marketplaces, Vendors, Customers
- Outcome: Helps reduce cancellations from stock errors.

#### 3PL inventory reconciliation
- Purpose: Fulfill through third-party warehouses
- Summary: Send shipping instructions to 3PL warehouses and reconcile receipts, shipments and inventory adjustments.
- Capabilities:
  - Warehouse orders sent electronically
  - Missing shipping confirmations flagged
  - Receipts, shipments and inventory reconciled across documents
- Parties: Suppliers, 3PLs, Retailers
- Outcome: Fewer inventory discrepancies with 3PLs.

### Ship and receive
Shipments tracked from dock to receipt.

#### Inbound shipment visibility
- Purpose: Coordinate inbound deliveries
- Summary: Follow routing requests, carrier tenders and status events in one transaction view, with timing rules monitored by agents.
- Capabilities:
  - Tender, status and appointment documents linked to the shipment
  - Missing delivery events detected as they occur
  - Timing rules set in plain language and monitored
- Parties: Suppliers, Carriers, Retailer DCs
- Outcome: Shared status on inbound shipments.

#### ASN intelligence
- Purpose: Resolve ship notice failures
- Summary: Monitor ship notice health by supplier, explain each rejection, and flag ASNs at risk of missing SLA.
- Capabilities:
  - ASN volumes, failures and SLA adherence by supplier
  - Rejections explained with the rule broken and the fix
  - Recurring supplier issues and at-risk ASNs flagged
- Parties: Retailers, Suppliers
- Outcome: Helps improve first-pass ASN acceptance.

#### Chargeback prevention alerts
- Purpose: Act before a penalty is assessed
- Summary: Alert supplier business users to pending shipments and invoice mismatches while the retailer's compliance window is still open.
- Capabilities:
  - Pending shipment alerts before the ship notice window closes
  - Invoice mismatch alerts by order, line and amount
  - Alerts routed to the business user who owns the order
- Parties: Suppliers, Retailers
- Outcome: Helps reduce avoidable chargebacks.

#### Receiving and three-way match
- Purpose: Match what arrived to what was billed
- Summary: See ship notice health by supplier, and compare orders, ship notices and invoices line by line before payment.
- Capabilities:
  - Ship notice health, failures and trends by supplier
  - Order, ship notice and invoice compared by SKU, quantity and price
  - Mismatched lines highlighted, with packing detail from pallet to item
- Parties: Retailers, Suppliers
- Outcome: Cleaner receiving and three-way match.

#### Direct store delivery reconciliation
- Purpose: Agree the count at the store
- Summary: Confirm delivered quantities at store check-in, invoice from that record, and track adjustments by store and item.
- Capabilities:
  - Delivery counts confirmed at check-in
  - Adjustments recorded at the store door
  - Adjustment trends by route, store and item
- Parties: DSD suppliers, Stores
- Outcome: Helps reduce store-level disputes.

### Settle and recover
Payments, deductions and credits resolved.

#### Chargeback management
- Purpose: Issue compliance chargebacks with evidence
- Summary: Capture vendor compliance violations, assess each against your terms, and issue chargebacks with the failing document and rule.
- Capabilities:
  - Violations captured from document data and on the receiving floor
  - Each violation assessed against vendor compliance terms, with its own workflow
  - Chargebacks issued with the failing document and rule, and vendor disputes tracked
- Parties: Retailers, Vendors
- Outcome: Compliance costs captured and tracked.

#### Deduction management
- Purpose: Recover invalid deductions
- Summary: Read deductions from remittances and debit memos, match each to its invoice and reason code, and dispute the invalid ones with the document trail.
- Capabilities:
  - Deductions from the 820 and 812 matched to the invoice and reason code
  - Status and amount for each deduction: assessed, pending, disputed, reversed or not charged
  - Disputes backed by the order, ship notice, invoice and proof of delivery
- Parties: Suppliers, Retailers
- Outcome: Helps recover invalid deductions.

#### Supplier compliance scorecard
- Purpose: Measure your own retailer compliance
- Summary: Score fill rate and document accuracy by retailer, with variance bands and period-over-period trends.
- Capabilities:
  - Fill rate, ship notice accuracy and ship notice timeliness by retailer
  - Invoice accuracy against the order and ship notice
  - Variance bands and period-over-period trends
- Parties: Suppliers, Retailers
- Outcome: Compliance measured before the retailer review.

#### Returns and credit management
- Purpose: Manage the reverse supply chain
- Summary: Authorize each return to the supplier, track it back, grade it on receipt, and settle the credit against the original return.
- Capabilities:
  - Returns authorized before they ship
  - Return credits matched to authorizations
  - Return credits and deductions without an authorization flagged
- Parties: Retailers, Suppliers, Carriers
- Outcome: Reverse supply chain, from authorization to credit.

## What OpenText provides
Connectivity, partner onboarding, visibility, analytics and AI agents across every retail process.

### Connect and onboard
- Pre-connected community: Reach suppliers, carriers and marketplaces already on the network.
- Self-service onboarding: Partners register, test documents against your rules and go live in a guided flow.
- One partner portal: A branded front door with single sign-on for suppliers and distributors.
- Web access for smaller suppliers: Suppliers without EDI receive orders and send ship notices, labels and invoices online.

### See and recover
- Transaction search and recovery: Find any document, follow its processing flow, and redeliver or reprocess it.
- Monitoring and anomaly detection: Daily digests, volume projections and alerts when traffic departs from normal.
- Community view: Every partner, relationship and document exchange, with the right contacts on each.
- e-Invoicing compliance: Compliant invoicing in more than 50 countries as a managed service.

### Measure and improve
- Agents that monitor your rules: Describe a rule in plain language; agents check transactions and explain each finding.
- Partner scorecards: Score suppliers on fulfillment, shipping and invoicing with weights you set.
- Ready-made retail analytics: Dashboards for shipment health, compliance and sell-through, with questions in plain language.
- Governed data delivery: Trusted network data explored in place or delivered to your own analytics on schedule.

### Act with AI agents
- Errors explained and routed: Agents read a document error, explain it in business terms and route it to its fix.
- Root cause across failures: Related failures grouped to one cause, with the follow-up to each partner drafted.
- Agents in your tools: Ask about orders, shipments and deductions from the assistants your teams already use.
- People approve every change: Agents investigate and recommend; a person approves any resend, update or ticket.

## Network
- 1M+: Trading partners on the OpenText network
- $11T: In annual commerce across the network
- 40+: Years of B2B integration experience

# Retail and CPG documents

Source: Business Network Process Genome, Process Genome for Retail and CPG (https://process-genome.onrender.com/#retail/map).
Status: Examples describe typical operating scenarios, not specific customer accounts. Standards, versions, and mandate dates vary by partner and region. Confirm requirements with each partner before building.

Code key: X12 set, or the EDIFACT or GDSN message where no X12 set exists. 41 documents, grouped by family in flow order.

## Item data

- **CIN Catalogue item notification**. Sender: Data pool. Receiver: Retailer. Europe and international: GDSN CIN. Delivers the supplier's published item data to a subscribing retailer. Used in: Item and price synchronization.
- **CIC Catalogue item confirmation**. Sender: Retailer. Receiver: Supplier, through the data pool. Europe and international: GDSN CIC. Retailer's response to an item notification: synchronized, accepted, review or rejected. Used in: Item and price synchronization.
- **832 Price and sales catalog**. Sender: Supplier. Receiver: Retailer. Europe and international: PRICAT. Item list with identifiers, descriptions and costs, sent at setup and on change. Used in: Item and price synchronization; Drop ship and marketplaces.
- **888 Item maintenance**. Sender: Supplier. Receiver: Retailer. Europe and international: PRODAT. Adds or changes item records. Used for DSD and grocery item authorization. Used in: Item and price synchronization; Direct store delivery.
- **879 Price information**. Sender: Supplier. Receiver: Retailer. Europe and international: PRICAT. Penalty-prone. Cost changes with effective dates. Late changes cause invoice price mismatches. Used in: Item and price synchronization; Direct store delivery.
- **889 Promotion announcement**. Sender: Supplier. Receiver: Retailer. No EDIFACT equivalent. Promotion terms, allowances and dates used later to settle deals. Used in: Item and price synchronization; Returns, credits and allowances.

## Plan

- **852 Product activity data**. Sender: Retailer. Receiver: Supplier. Europe and international: SLSRPT, INVRPT. Sales and on-hand inventory by item and location. The input to replenishment and sales analytics. Used in: Direct store delivery; Vendor-managed inventory and CPFR; Sales and inventory reporting.
- **830 Planning schedule**. Sender: Retailer. Receiver: Supplier. Europe and international: SLSFCT. Forecast quantities by item and period for supply planning. Used in: Vendor-managed inventory and CPFR.
- **846 Inventory advice**. Sender: Supplier or 3PL. Receiver: Retailer or supplier. Europe and international: INVRPT. Penalty-prone. Available quantity by item. In drop ship it decides what the retailer can sell. Used in: Drop ship and marketplaces; 3PL fulfillment.

## Order

- **850 Purchase order**. Sender: Retailer. Receiver: Supplier. Europe and international: ORDERS. Items, quantities, cost, ship window and ship-to location. Used in: Order to cash; Item and price synchronization; Drop ship and marketplaces; 3PL fulfillment; Vendor onboarding and certification.
- **855 Order acknowledgment**. Sender: Supplier. Receiver: Retailer. Europe and international: ORDRSP. Penalty-prone. Accepts, changes or rejects each order line before shipment. Used in: Order to cash; Vendor-managed inventory and CPFR; Drop ship and marketplaces; Vendor onboarding and certification.
- **860 Order change**. Sender: Retailer. Receiver: Supplier. Europe and international: ORDCHG. Changes quantities, dates or lines on an open order. Used in: Order to cash; Drop ship and marketplaces.
- **865 Change acknowledgment**. Sender: Supplier. Receiver: Retailer. Europe and international: ORDRSP. Accepts or rejects the retailer's order change. Used in: Order to cash; Drop ship and marketplaces.
- **870 Order status**. Sender: Supplier. Receiver: Retailer. No EDIFACT equivalent. Status of open orders. Used in drop ship for backorders and cancellations. Used in: Drop ship and marketplaces.

## Move

- **753 Routing request**. Sender: Supplier. Receiver: Retailer. No EDIFACT equivalent. Penalty-prone. Ready-to-ship details (cartons, weight and cube) with a request for a carrier. Used in: Routing and delivery.
- **754 Routing instructions**. Sender: Retailer. Receiver: Supplier. No EDIFACT equivalent. Assigned carrier, load and pickup details for the shipment. Used in: Routing and delivery.
- **204 Load tender**. Sender: Retailer. Receiver: Carrier. Europe and international: IFTMIN. Offers a load to a carrier with stops, dates and references. Used in: Routing and delivery.
- **990 Tender response**. Sender: Carrier. Receiver: Retailer. No EDIFACT equivalent. Carrier accepts or declines the tendered load. Used in: Routing and delivery.
- **211 Bill of lading**. Sender: Supplier. Receiver: Carrier. Europe and international: IFTMIN. Electronic bill of lading for the shipment. Used in: Routing and delivery.
- **214 Shipment status**. Sender: Carrier. Receiver: Retailer. Europe and international: IFTSTA. Penalty-prone. Pickup, in-transit, appointment and delivery events. Used in: Routing and delivery.

## Ship and confirm

- **856 Ship notice**. Sender: Supplier. Receiver: Retailer. Europe and international: DESADV. Penalty-prone. Shipment, order, carton and item detail with SSCC labels, sent before arrival. Used in: Order to cash; Receive, match and pay; Routing and delivery; Vendor-managed inventory and CPFR; Drop ship and marketplaces; 3PL fulfillment; Vendor onboarding and certification; Compliance chargebacks.
- **997 Functional acknowledgment**. Sender: Either party. Receiver: Either party. Europe and international: CONTRL. Confirms receipt and syntax. It does not confirm business acceptance. Used in: Order to cash; Receive, match and pay; Drop ship and marketplaces; Sales and inventory reporting; Vendor onboarding and certification.
- **824 Application advice**. Sender: Retailer. Receiver: Supplier. Europe and international: APERAK. Penalty-prone. Accepts or rejects a received document, with reason codes. Used in: Order to cash; Receive, match and pay; Direct store delivery; Vendor-managed inventory and CPFR; Drop ship and marketplaces; Vendor onboarding and certification.
- **864 Text message**. Sender: Retailer. Receiver: Supplier. Europe and international: GENRAL. Free-form notice from the retailer, such as a document rejection, compliance notice or chargeback notice. Used in: Order to cash; Receive, match and pay; Deductions and disputes; Compliance chargebacks.
- **861 Receiving advice**. Sender: Retailer. Receiver: Supplier. Europe and international: RECADV. Accepted and rejected quantities after receipt, with reasons. Sent by some retailers only. Used in: Receive, match and pay; Compliance chargebacks.

## Settle

- **810 Invoice**. Sender: Supplier. Receiver: Retailer. Europe and international: INVOIC. Penalty-prone. Bills shipped quantities at the agreed cost and terms. Used in: Order to cash; Receive, match and pay; Deductions and disputes; Direct store delivery; Vendor-managed inventory and CPFR; Drop ship and marketplaces; 3PL fulfillment; Returns, credits and allowances; Vendor onboarding and certification.
- **820 Remittance**. Sender: Retailer. Receiver: Supplier. Europe and international: REMADV. Penalty-prone. Payment detail by invoice, including deductions with reason codes. Used in: Order to cash; Receive, match and pay; Deductions and disputes; Direct store delivery; Drop ship and marketplaces; Returns, credits and allowances; Compliance chargebacks.
- **812 Credit or debit memo**. Sender: Retailer for debits, supplier for credits. Receiver: The other party. Europe and international: COMDIS. Penalty-prone. Debits or credits against invoices for shortages, violations, returns and allowances. Used in: Receive, match and pay; Deductions and disputes; Returns, credits and allowances; Compliance chargebacks.
- **210 Freight invoice**. Sender: Carrier. Receiver: Retailer. Europe and international: INVOIC. Carrier bill for a delivered load. Used in: Routing and delivery.

## Return

- **180 Return authorization**. Sender: Retailer requests, supplier authorizes. Receiver: The other party. Europe and international: RETANN, RETINS. Requests and authorizes a return, with disposition instructions. Used in: Returns, credits and allowances.

## Grocery and DSD series

- **875 Grocery order**. Sender: Retailer. Receiver: Supplier. Europe and international: ORDERS. Purchase order format used in grocery and foodservice. Used in: Order to cash.
- **876 Grocery order change**. Sender: Retailer. Receiver: Supplier. Europe and international: ORDCHG. Changes an open grocery order. Used in: Order to cash.
- **880 Grocery invoice**. Sender: Supplier. Receiver: Retailer. Europe and international: INVOIC. Penalty-prone. Invoice format used in grocery and foodservice. Used in: Order to cash; Receive, match and pay.
- **894 DSD delivery record**. Sender: DSD supplier. Receiver: Store. No EDIFACT equivalent. Penalty-prone. Itemized delivery the store checks at the back door. Used in: Direct store delivery.
- **895 DSD adjustment**. Sender: Store. Receiver: DSD supplier. No EDIFACT equivalent. Store accepts or adjusts the delivery record. Used in: Direct store delivery.
- **882 DSD summary**. Sender: DSD supplier. Receiver: Retailer. No EDIFACT equivalent. Summary of store deliveries for settlement. Used in: Direct store delivery.

## Warehouse series

- **940 Warehouse shipping order**. Sender: Supplier. Receiver: 3PL. Europe and international: INSDES. Instructs the 3PL to pick and ship an order. Used in: 3PL fulfillment.
- **945 Warehouse shipping advice**. Sender: 3PL. Receiver: Supplier. Europe and international: DESADV. Penalty-prone. Confirms what the 3PL shipped. Used in: 3PL fulfillment.
- **943 Stock transfer advice**. Sender: Supplier. Receiver: 3PL. Europe and international: DESADV. Tells the 3PL that inbound stock is on the way. Used in: 3PL fulfillment.
- **944 Stock transfer receipt**. Sender: 3PL. Receiver: Supplier. Europe and international: RECADV. Confirms the stock the 3PL received. Used in: 3PL fulfillment.
- **947 Inventory adjustment**. Sender: 3PL. Receiver: Supplier. Europe and international: INVRPT. Reports damage, count and status changes to 3PL stock. Used in: 3PL fulfillment.

File: https://process-genome.onrender.com/agents/automotive-solutions.txt

# Automotive solutions on Trading Grid

Source: Business Network Process Genome, Solution overview for Automotive (https://process-genome.onrender.com/#automotive/solution).
Status: Concept preview for internal review. Diagrams are illustrative. Some capabilities shown are in development or planned and are not generally available. Results depend on implementation and partner participation. Names, scope and availability may change.

OEM and supplier trading relationships, connected and managed. Integrate and onboard the OEMs, supplier tiers and logistics providers you trade with on Trading Grid, and monitor every release, ship notice and settlement.

## Solutions by stage

- Plan and release: Release management; Sub-tier supplier collaboration
- Ship and deliver: ASN and label compliance; Just-in-sequence monitoring; Inbound freight visibility
- Receive and settle: Cumulative quantity reconciliation; Self-billing and debit memo management
- Assets and aftermarket: Returnable container management; Aftermarket parts data and order management

### Plan and release
Schedules and sub-tier releases aligned before parts ship.

#### Release management
- Purpose: Act on every release change
- Summary: Load planning and shipping schedules as they arrive, compare each release with the last, and flag changes inside firm periods.
- Capabilities:
  - Release changes compared release over release, by part and plant
  - Changes inside firm periods or above agreed limits flagged
  - Missing or late schedules detected before the shipping window
- Parties: OEMs, Suppliers
- Outcome: Release changes visible before parts ship.

#### Sub-tier supplier collaboration
- Purpose: Extend release discipline to sub-tiers
- Summary: Issue your own releases to sub-tier suppliers as OEM demand changes, and hold them to the ship notice and settlement rules the OEM applies to you.
- Capabilities:
  - Releases issued to sub-tier suppliers as OEM demand changes
  - Web access for sub-tier suppliers without EDI
  - Sub-tier scorecards on timeliness and accuracy
- Parties: Tier 1 suppliers, Sub-tier suppliers
- Outcome: Sub-tier suppliers on the same rules.

### Ship and deliver
Ship notices, sequences and freight tracked to the plant.

#### ASN and label compliance
- Purpose: Send an accepted ship notice for every shipment
- Summary: Check each ship notice against the customer's guide before it leaves, match it to labels and the carrier pickup, and act on rejections quickly.
- Capabilities:
  - Ship notices validated against each customer's guide
  - Notices matched to labels and the carrier pickup
  - Rejections explained with the field to correct
- Parties: Suppliers, Carriers, OEM plants
- Outcome: Fewer ship notice debits.

#### Just-in-sequence monitoring
- Purpose: Deliver parts in build order
- Summary: Receive sequence messages as vehicles pass the broadcast point, track each build against its delivery window, and alert on gaps in the sequence.
- Capabilities:
  - Sequence messages monitored for gaps and delays
  - Sequence ship notices matched to the vehicles they supply
  - Plant-critical alerts routed to on-call teams
- Parties: Sequencing suppliers, Assembly plants
- Outcome: Earlier warning of sequence gaps.

#### Inbound freight visibility
- Purpose: Collect parts in the planned window
- Summary: Follow routing instructions, tenders and status events for each inbound shipment, and flag the risks that lead to premium freight.
- Capabilities:
  - Tenders, status events and freight bills linked to the shipment
  - Missed pickup windows flagged as they occur
  - Freight bills compared with tendered rates
- Parties: Suppliers, Logistics providers, Carriers
- Outcome: Earlier warning of premium freight.

### Receive and settle
Receipts, cums and payments reconciled.

#### Cumulative quantity reconciliation
- Purpose: Keep cum totals in agreement
- Summary: Compare shipped and received cumulative quantities by part, and resolve differences before they reach payment or balance-out.
- Capabilities:
  - Supplier and OEM cums compared from ship notices, receipts and the cum on each release
  - Differences traced to the ship notices and receipts behind them
  - Cum resets and balance-out claims supported with history
- Parties: Suppliers, OEMs
- Outcome: Fewer quantity disputes at reconciliation.

#### Self-billing and debit memo management
- Purpose: Get paid for every receipt
- Summary: Match receipts, self-billed invoices and remittances to shipments, and work debit memos inside their dispute windows.
- Capabilities:
  - Receipts and settlements matched to ship notices
  - Short payments and debit memos linked to the shipment
  - Dispute windows tracked with evidence attached
- Parties: OEMs, Suppliers
- Outcome: Fewer debits left open past their dispute window.

### Assets and aftermarket
Container balances reconciled and aftermarket product data kept current.

#### Returnable container management
- Purpose: Keep the container account in balance
- Summary: Track returnable container shipments, receipts and balances by type and site, and reconcile them before the periodic count.
- Capabilities:
  - Container movements tracked from ship notices
  - Balances by container type and site
  - Differences flagged before the periodic count
- Parties: OEMs, Suppliers
- Outcome: Container balances you can reconcile.

#### Aftermarket parts data and order management
- Purpose: Ship the right part with the right data
- Summary: Keep product and fitment data current with distributors, retailers and dealers, confirm orders, and reduce deductions.
- Capabilities:
  - Product and fitment data checked before it is published
  - Orders, acknowledgments and ship notices monitored by customer
  - Deductions linked to the order and shipment
- Parties: Parts suppliers, Distributors, Dealers
- Outcome: Cleaner orders from current product data.

## What OpenText provides
Connectivity, supplier onboarding, visibility, analytics and AI agents across automotive processes.

### Connect and onboard
- Automotive connectivity: OFTP2, AS2 and VAN connections to OEMs and suppliers, with certificates managed.
- Pre-connected community: Reach OEMs, suppliers and carriers already on the network.
- Guided supplier onboarding: Pre-built templates and APIs, with documents tested against each customer's guide.
- Web access for smaller suppliers: Suppliers without EDI receive schedules, send ship notices and invoices, and print labels online.

### See and recover
- Transaction search and recovery: Find any document, follow its processing flow, and redeliver or reprocess it.
- Plant-critical monitoring: Alerts when an expected schedule or ship notice is late for a plant's cutoff.
- Part traceability: Search lot and serial numbers from ship notices to support recall and quality investigations.
- E-invoicing compliance: Invoices issued in the formats tax authorities require in supported countries, as a managed service.

### Measure and improve
- Agents that monitor your rules: Describe a rule in plain language; agents check transactions and explain each finding.
- Supplier delivery scorecards: Score suppliers on release adherence, ship notice accuracy and on-time delivery.
- Ready-made automotive analytics: Dashboards for release volatility, cum differences and ship notice health.
- Governed data delivery: Network data explored in place or delivered to your own analytics on a schedule.

### Act with AI agents
- Errors explained and routed: Agents read a document error, explain it in business terms and route it to the team that fixes it.
- Root cause across failures: Related failures grouped to one cause, with the follow-up to each partner drafted.
- Agents in your tools: Ask about releases, shipments and debits from the assistants your teams already use.
- People approve every change: Agents investigate and recommend; a person approves any resend, update or ticket.

- 1M+: Trading partners on the OpenText network
- $11T: In annual commerce across the network
- 40+: Years of B2B integration experience

# Automotive documents

Source: Business Network Process Genome, Process Genome for Automotive (https://process-genome.onrender.com/#automotive/map).
Status: Examples describe typical operating scenarios, not specific customer accounts. Standards, versions, and mandate dates vary by partner and region. Confirm requirements with each partner before building.

Code key: X12 set, or the EDIFACT or VDA message where no X12 set exists. 25 documents, grouped by family in flow order.

## Catalog

- **832 Price and sales catalog**. Sender: Supplier. Receiver: Aftermarket buyer. Europe and international: PRICAT. Part list with identifiers, descriptions and prices, sent at setup and on change. Fitment and attribute data travel separately as files. Used in: Aftermarket order to cash.

## Order

- **850 Purchase order**. Sender: Customer. Receiver: Supplier. Europe and international: ORDERS. Blanket order setting price, terms and ship-to per part, or a spot order in the aftermarket. Used in: Forecast and release; Sub-tier procurement; Aftermarket order to cash.
- **860 Purchase order change**. Sender: Customer. Receiver: Supplier. Europe and international: ORDCHG. Changes price, part, engineering level or terms on an open blanket order. Used in: Forecast and release; Sub-tier procurement.
- **855 Order acknowledgment**. Sender: Supplier. Receiver: Customer. Europe and international: ORDRSP. Confirms each order line, with substitutions for superseded parts and ship dates. Used in: Aftermarket order to cash.

## Plan and release

- **830 Planning schedule**. Sender: Customer. Receiver: Supplier. Europe and international: DELFOR. Odette DELINS. VDA 4984, replacing VDA 4905. Forecast by part and ship-to with firm and planning periods, cum received, and fabrication and material authorizations. Used in: Forecast and release; Cumulative reconciliation and balance-out; Just in sequence; Sub-tier procurement.
- **862 Shipping schedule**. Sender: Customer. Receiver: Supplier. Europe and international: DELJIT. Odette CALDEL. VDA 4985, which with VDA 4984 replaces VDA 4915. Penalty-prone. Near-term ship or delivery quantities and dates that supersede the forecast's near-term ship data. Used in: Forecast and release; Sub-tier procurement.
- **866 Production sequence**. Sender: Customer. Receiver: Sequencing supplier. Europe and international: DELJIT. Odette SYNCRO. VDA 4986, replacing VDA 4916. Penalty-prone. Build sequence by vehicle: identifier, sequence number, variant, assembly point and time of use. Used in: Just in sequence.
- **846 Inventory advice**. Sender: Supplier. Receiver: Customer. Europe and international: INVRPT. Available quantity by part. In aftermarket drop ship it sets what the buyer can promise. Used in: Aftermarket order to cash.

## Ship and confirm

- **856 Ship notice**. Sender: Supplier. Receiver: Customer. Europe and international: DESADV. Odette AVIEXP. VDA 4987, replacing VDA 4913. Penalty-prone. Shipment, bill of lading, parts, quantities, cum shipped, packaging and container serials that match the labels. Used in: Forecast and release; Cumulative reconciliation and balance-out; Ship notice and labels; Just in sequence; Receipt and settlement; Inbound transport; Sub-tier procurement; Aftermarket order to cash; Returnable containers.
- **997 Functional acknowledgment**. Sender: Either party. Receiver: Either party. Europe and international: CONTRL. Confirms receipt and syntax. It does not confirm business acceptance. Used in: Forecast and release; Ship notice and labels; Sub-tier procurement.
- **824 Application advice**. Sender: Customer. Receiver: Supplier. Europe and international: APERAK. VDA 4937. Penalty-prone. Accepts or rejects a ship notice or invoice, with error detail. Used in: Ship notice and labels; Receipt and settlement.

## Move

- **204 Load tender**. Sender: Lead logistics provider. Receiver: Carrier. Europe and international: IFTMIN. VDA 4933. Offers a planned load to a carrier with stops, windows and load number. Used in: Inbound transport.
- **990 Tender response**. Sender: Carrier. Receiver: Lead logistics provider. Europe and international: VDA 4933 covers the transport order confirmation. Carrier accepts or declines the tendered load. Used in: Inbound transport.
- **214 Shipment status**. Sender: Carrier. Receiver: Lead logistics provider or booking party. Europe and international: IFTSTA. VDA 4945. Penalty-prone. Pickup, in-transit and delivery events against the load and bill of lading. Used in: Ship notice and labels; Inbound transport.
- **210 Freight invoice**. Sender: Carrier. Receiver: Bill-to party. Europe and international: INVOIC. VDA 4938 part 4 covers the freight invoice. Carrier bill for a delivered load, audited against the tender. Used in: Inbound transport.

## Receive and settle

- **861 Receiving advice**. Sender: Customer. Receiver: Supplier. Europe and international: RECADV. VDA 4989 uses it as the entry certificate for intra-EU deliveries. Penalty-prone. Reports receipt differences: over, short, no notice, returns, scrap and cum adjustments. Used in: Cumulative reconciliation and balance-out; Receipt and settlement.
- **810 Invoice**. Sender: Supplier. Receiver: Customer. Europe and international: INVOIC. VDA 4938, replacing VDA 4906. Penalty-prone. Bills a shipment where the customer does not pay from receipts. Used in: Receipt and settlement; Sub-tier procurement; Aftermarket order to cash.
- **INVOIC Self-billing invoice**. Sender: Customer. Receiver: Supplier. Europe and international: EDIFACT INVOIC. VDA 4938, replacing VDA 4908. No X12 set. Penalty-prone. The customer's invoice for the supply, built from its receipts and agreed price; the supplier's tax record. Used in: Receipt and settlement; Sub-tier procurement.
- **820 Remittance advice**. Sender: Customer. Receiver: Supplier. Europe and international: REMADV. VDA 4988, replacing VDA 4907. Penalty-prone. Payment detail by receipt or invoice, net of debits, with reason codes. Used in: Receipt and settlement; Sub-tier procurement; Aftermarket order to cash.

## Return

- **180 Return authorization**. Sender: Buyer requests, supplier authorizes. Receiver: The other party. Europe and international: RETANN, RETINS. Requests and authorizes a parts return, with disposition. Used in: Aftermarket order to cash.

## Container series

- **4946 Container order**. Sender: Supplier or container owner. Receiver: The other party. Europe and international: VDA 4946. No X12 set. Orders empty returnable containers and confirms the order. Used in: Returnable containers.
- **4943 Empties despatch advice**. Sender: Container owner. Receiver: Supplier. Europe and international: VDA 4943. No X12 set. Forecasts and announces empty container shipments to the supplier. Used in: Returnable containers.
- **4947 Container movement**. Sender: Supplier. Receiver: Container owner. Europe and international: VDA 4947. No X12 set. Penalty-prone. Confirms empties received and books container movements. Used in: Returnable containers.
- **4941 Container account statement**. Sender: Container owner. Receiver: Supplier. Europe and international: VDA 4941. No X12 set. Penalty-prone. Periodic statement of bookings and closing balance per container type. Used in: Returnable containers.
- **4942 Container inventory**. Sender: Supplier. Receiver: Container owner. Europe and international: VDA 4942. No X12 set. Penalty-prone. Container count on hand by type and site, usually at year end, with any differences. Used in: Returnable containers.

# Financial services solutions on Trading Grid

Source: Business Network Process Genome, Solution overview for Financial services (https://process-genome.onrender.com/#banking/solution).
Status: Concept preview for internal review. Diagrams are illustrative. Some capabilities shown are in development or planned and are not generally available. Results depend on implementation and partner participation. Figures are as published by OpenText. Names, scope and availability may change.

Bank and corporate relationships, connected and managed. Connect the banks, corporate clients, payment networks and market participants you work with on Trading Grid, and monitor every payment, statement and confirmation.

## Solutions by stage

- Connect and pay: Corporate onboarding and connectivity; Corporate payment initiation; Instant payments and request to pay; Supplier payment and remittance delivery
- Collect and report: Direct debit collection management; Receivables and cash application; Statement and cash reporting
- Screen and resolve: Sanctions screening and fraud controls; Payment status and returns management; Payment tracking and investigations
- Cross-border and markets: Cross-border payments and ISO 20022 transformation; Trade finance and FX confirmation; Fund order processing; Securities settlement and custody messaging

### Connect and pay
Clients connected and payments initiated on every channel.

#### Corporate onboarding and connectivity
- Purpose: Bring each client live on its channel
- Summary: Set up Swift, EBICS, host-to-host or API channels for each corporate client, build maps, and test files before go-live.
- Capabilities:
  - Channel, keys and certificates set up per client
  - Test files validated against the bank's formats
  - Onboarding status tracked from request to first live file
- Parties: Banks, Corporate clients
- Outcome: Shorter onboarding for corporate clients.

#### Corporate payment initiation
- Purpose: Catch payment file errors before the bank does
- Summary: Validate payment files against schema and bank rules before release, and track each file to its status report.
- Capabilities:
  - Files checked against ISO 20022, Nacha and bank-specific rules
  - Cutoffs monitored by payment method and value date
  - Rejected files explained with the field to correct
- Parties: Corporates, Banks
- Outcome: Fewer rejected payment files.

#### Instant payments and request to pay
- Purpose: Know instant payment status in seconds
- Summary: Route instant credit transfers and request-to-pay messages, and track each one to its final status within scheme time limits.
- Capabilities:
  - Instant transfers tracked to accept or reject
  - Request-to-pay responses matched to the request
  - Timeouts and rejects flagged as they occur
- Parties: Banks, Instant schemes
- Outcome: Instant payment status in real time.

#### Supplier payment and remittance delivery
- Purpose: Send remittance detail with every payment
- Summary: Carry structured remittance with supplier payments, and deliver remittance advice that suppliers can apply automatically.
- Capabilities:
  - Structured remittance carried in the payment
  - Remittance advice delivered in each supplier's format
  - Unapplied supplier payments traced to the remittance
- Parties: Corporates, Banks, Suppliers
- Outcome: Fewer supplier payment inquiries.

### Collect and report
Collections, receipts and balances reported and applied.

#### Direct debit collection management
- Purpose: Collect on the due date
- Summary: Submit collections against valid mandates, and handle returns and rejections inside scheme timelines.
- Capabilities:
  - Collections checked against mandates before submission
  - Returns and rejects matched to the original collection
  - Return reasons reported by debtor and reason
- Parties: Creditors, Banks, Debtors
- Outcome: Fewer returned collections.

#### Receivables and cash application
- Purpose: Apply incoming cash to open invoices
- Summary: Combine lockbox, remittance and credit notifications, and match payments to open receivables.
- Capabilities:
  - Lockbox, remittance and credit notifications combined
  - Payments matched to open invoices by reference
  - Unapplied cash flagged with the missing detail
- Parties: Corporates, Banks
- Outcome: Less unapplied cash.

#### Statement and cash reporting
- Purpose: Deliver balances before treasury needs them
- Summary: Collect prior-day and intraday statements from every bank, convert them to one format, and flag missing reports.
- Capabilities:
  - Statements in BAI2, camt and MT formats normalized
  - Missing or late statements flagged by bank and account
  - Balances available for daily cash positioning
- Parties: Banks, Corporate treasury
- Outcome: Complete daily cash position.

### Screen and resolve
Payments screened, rejected items returned and cases closed.

#### Sanctions screening and fraud controls
- Purpose: Screen payments inside the flow
- Summary: Screen payments against sanctions lists before release, hold matches for review, and monitor for fraud patterns.
- Capabilities:
  - Screening embedded before payment release
  - Held payments routed for review and decision
  - Unusual payment patterns flagged for investigation
- Parties: Banks, Corporates
- Outcome: Screening without leaving the payment flow.

#### Payment status and returns management
- Purpose: Know the status of every payment
- Summary: Collect status reports, returns and change notifications, and link each one to the original payment.
- Capabilities:
  - Status reports linked to the original payment
  - Returns and notifications of change routed to the owner
  - Return trends by reason and beneficiary bank
- Parties: Banks, Corporates
- Outcome: Rejected payments found the same day.

#### Payment tracking and investigations
- Purpose: Close payment cases faster
- Summary: Track cross-border payments end to end, and manage cancellation requests and inquiries with their responses.
- Capabilities:
  - Payment progress tracked across banks
  - Cancellation requests matched to their resolution
  - Open cases aged by bank and reason
- Parties: Banks, Correspondents
- Outcome: Fewer open payment investigations.

### Cross-border and markets
Correspondent, trade, fund and securities flows.

#### Cross-border payments and ISO 20022 transformation
- Purpose: Send cross-border payments in ISO 20022
- Summary: Transform between MT and ISO 20022 formats, validate rich data, and route payments through correspondents.
- Capabilities:
  - MT and ISO 20022 messages transformed and validated
  - Truncation and data loss flagged before sending
  - Payment progress followed across correspondents
- Parties: Banks, Correspondents
- Outcome: Truncation risk flagged before payments leave.

#### Trade finance and FX confirmation
- Purpose: Exchange trade and FX messages with banks
- Summary: Send and receive letters of credit, guarantees and amendments, and match FX confirmations to trades.
- Capabilities:
  - Letter of credit and guarantee messages exchanged with banks
  - Amendments linked to the original instrument
  - FX confirmations matched to the trade
- Parties: Corporates, Banks
- Outcome: Trade and FX messages in one view.

#### Fund order processing
- Purpose: Process fund orders to confirmation
- Summary: Route subscription, redemption and switch orders to transfer agents, and match each order to its confirmation.
- Capabilities:
  - Orders validated before cutoff
  - Confirmations matched to the original order
  - Unconfirmed orders flagged by fund and agent
- Parties: Distributors, Transfer agents
- Outcome: Fewer unconfirmed fund orders.

#### Securities settlement and custody messaging
- Purpose: Settle trades on the intended date
- Summary: Send settlement instructions to custodians, follow their status, and reconcile confirmations and holdings.
- Capabilities:
  - Settlement instructions validated before sending
  - Status and confirmations linked to each instruction
  - Holdings statements reconciled to internal positions
- Parties: Investment managers, Custodians
- Outcome: Fewer failed settlements.

## What OpenText provides
Bank connectivity, message transformation, controls, visibility and AI agents across financial services flows.

### Connect and onboard
- Bank connectivity: Swift, EBICS, host-to-host and API channels, with keys and certificates managed.
- Managed Swift access: Swift connectivity as a managed service, without in-house infrastructure.
- Corporate client onboarding: Connectivity setup, map development and end-to-end testing for each new client.
- Large file exchange: Managed file transfer for high-volume and large files.

### Transform and control
- ISO 20022 transformation: Conversion between MT, ISO 20022, Nacha, BAI2 and ERP formats, with validation.
- Embedded sanctions screening: Screening inside the payment flow, with alerts on held payments.
- Fraud monitoring: Payment patterns monitored for anomalies before release.
- Release controls: Value limits and multilevel approval on payment release.

### See and measure
- Transaction lifecycle tracking: Payments and statements traced from file receipt to final status.
- Payments portal: Clients submit instructions and follow status in a web portal.
- Bank and client scorecards: Acceptance rates, reject reasons and cutoff adherence by bank and client.
- Governed data delivery: Network data explored in place or delivered to your own analytics on a schedule.

### Act with AI agents
- Errors explained and routed: Agents read a reject or return, explain it in business terms and route it to the team that fixes it.
- Root cause across failures: Related rejects grouped to one cause, with the follow-up to each bank or client drafted.
- Agents in your tools: Ask about payment status, returns and statements from the assistants your teams already use.
- Approval before change: Agents investigate and recommend; a person approves resends, releases and updates.

- 30+: Years supporting financial services
- 14 of 15: Largest North American banks run transactions on the network
- 31B+: Transactions processed each year
